title: Algorithms and Coding
intro: Algorithms, bugs, loops and how computers follow instructions.

questions.prompt: What is an algorithm?

options.label: A set of step-by-step instructions to solve a problem

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a list of steps, in the right order, for completing a task or solving a problem.

questions.prompt: What do we call a mistake in a computer program?
questions.explanation: A mistake in a program is called a bug.

questions.prompt: What is it called when you find and fix mistakes in a program?
questions.explanation: Debugging means finding and fixing the bugs in a program so it works properly.

questions.prompt: What do we call a part of a program that repeats instructions?
questions.explanation: A loop repeats instructions, which saves writing the same steps again and again.

questions.prompt: Carrying out instructions one after another, in order, is called…
questions.explanation: Sequence means following steps in the right order. Getting the order wrong can change the result.

questions.prompt: Using "if" to choose what a program does next is called…
questions.explanation: Selection lets a program make a choice: if something is true, do one thing; otherwise do another.

questions.prompt: A computer can only follow the instructions it has been given.
questions.explanation: Computers do exactly what their programs tell them, which is why clear, correct algorithms matter.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a block-based programming language often used in schools?
questions.explanation: Scratch lets you snap together coding blocks to make animations, stories and games.

questions.prompt: In an algorithm, the order of the steps never matters.
questions.explanation: The order matters. Putting on your shoes before your socks would not work!

questions.prompt: In a program, what is a variable?

options.label: A named place that stores a value which can change

questions.explanation: A variable is like a labelled box. A game might use a variable called score and change its value each time you win a point.

questions.prompt: In Scratch, what are the characters and objects that you program called?
questions.explanation: In Scratch, sprites are the characters and objects on the stage. You snap blocks together to tell each sprite what to do.

questions.prompt: A robot follows this code: repeat 4 times, move forward 2 steps. How many steps does it move in total?
questions.explanation: The loop runs 4 times and the robot moves 2 steps each time, so it moves 4 × 2 = 8 steps.

questions.prompt: Which instructions would make a sprite draw a square?

options.label: Repeat 6 times: move 50 steps, turn 60 degrees
Repeat 3 times: move 50 steps, turn 120 degrees
Repeat 4 times: move 50 steps, turn 45 degrees
Repeat 4 times: move 50 steps, turn 90 degrees

questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles, so you repeat 'move, then turn 90 degrees' four times.

questions.prompt: What does a 'forever' loop do?

options.label: Repeats its instructions until the program is stopped

questions.explanation: A forever loop keeps going round and round. Games often use one to keep checking for key presses.

questions.prompt: Using a loop can save you from writing the same instruction lots of times.
questions.explanation: Instead of writing 'move' ten times, you can put 'move' inside a loop that repeats ten times. It is shorter and easier to fix.

questions.prompt: The code says: if it is raining, take an umbrella, else wear sunglasses. What happens when it is NOT raining?
questions.explanation: When the 'if' condition is false, the program follows the 'else' part instead. This choosing is called selection.

questions.prompt: Breaking a big problem down into smaller, easier parts is called…
questions.explanation: Decomposition makes hard problems easier. To program a game, you might work on the player, the score and the levels one at a time.

questions.prompt: A program shows the message 'Well done!' on the screen when you win. This message is an example of…
questions.explanation: An output is what a program gives back to you, such as words on a screen or a sound. What you type or click is the input.

questions.prompt: What does a search engine help you to do?

options.label: Find web pages about a topic

questions.explanation: A search engine looks through a huge list of web pages and shows you the ones that match the words you typed.

questions.prompt: Everything you read on a website is sure to be true.
questions.explanation: Anyone can put things online, so not everything is true. It is smart to check facts on more than one trusted website.

questions.prompt: Which of these should you keep private when you are online?

options.label: The name of a book you like

questions.explanation: Personal details such as your address, school or phone number should stay private. If you are unsure, ask a trusted adult.

questions.prompt: What is a computer network?

options.label: A game played on one computer
Computers joined together so they can share information
A computer that has no screen

questions.explanation: When computers are linked, by cables or wirelessly, they form a network and can share files, printers and messages.

questions.prompt: Which of these best describes the internet?

options.label: A huge network that links computers all around the world

questions.explanation: The internet joins millions of networks together, so computers on opposite sides of the world can send data to each other.

questions.prompt: What does a 'repeat until' loop do?

options.label: Repeats some steps until a condition becomes true

questions.explanation: A 'repeat until' loop checks a condition each time. For example, 'repeat until touching the wall' stops as soon as the sprite reaches the wall.

questions.prompt: In a program, what does the condition 'score > 10' check?

options.label: Whether the score is more than 10
Whether the score is less than 10

questions.explanation: The > sign means 'greater than'. The condition is true when the score is 11 or more.

questions.prompt: A counter starts at 0. A loop adds 3 to the counter each time it runs. What is the counter after the loop runs 5 times?
questions.explanation: The counter goes 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. Adding 3 five times is the same as 5 × 3 = 15.

questions.prompt: Your sprite should move right, but it moves left. What is the best thing to do first?

options.label: Read through the code step by step to find the bug

questions.explanation: Debugging means carefully checking each step to find what went wrong. Here a direction or number is probably the wrong way round.

questions.prompt: In Scratch, which group of blocks contains the 'if … then' block?
questions.explanation: The orange Control blocks include loops and 'if … then' blocks, which control the order things happen in.

questions.prompt: Two different algorithms can both solve the same problem correctly.
questions.explanation: There is often more than one way to solve a problem. Programmers compare algorithms to find the quickest or simplest one.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to 'run' a program?

options.label: To type the program very fast
To make the computer carry out its instructions
To print the program on paper

questions.explanation: When you run a program, the computer follows its instructions in order. In Scratch, clicking the green flag runs your project.
